problem.title: Certification-Gated Earliest Enrollment Date Lookup
problem.prompt: You are building a learner engagement dashboard. For each course, you need to find the earliest enrollment date among all students who enrolled in that course, but ONLY display this date if the course has been certified by the platform (certification_approved = TRUE). If a course is not certified, output NULL for the earliest enrollment date instead of excluding the course from results. The output should have one row per course with columns: course_id, course_name, certification_approved, earliest_enrollment. Order results by course_id ascending. Courses may have zero, one, or many enrollments; handle all cases correctly.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE courses (course_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, course_name VARCHAR(100), certification_approved BOOLEAN); CREATE TABLE enrollments (enrollment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, course_id INTEGER, student_id INTEGER, enrollment_date DATE);
problem.example_input_data: INSERT INTO courses (course_id, course_name, certification_approved) VALUES (101, 'Introduction to SQL', TRUE), (102, 'Advanced Python', FALSE), (103, 'Data Structures', TRUE), (104, 'Machine Learning Basics', FALSE); INSERT INTO enrollments (enrollment_id, course_id, student_id, enrollment_date) VALUES (1, 101, 1001, '2024-01-15'), (2, 101, 1002, '2024-01-10'), (3, 101, 1003, '2024-01-20'), (4, 102, 1004, '2024-02-05'), (5, 102, 1005, '2024-02-01'), (6, 103, 1006, '2024-03-12'), (7, 104, 1007, '2024-04-08');

composite_moves: lookup gate attribute (certification_approved) from courses table
compute per-entity pick (MIN enrollment_date per course) from enrollments table
apply gate via CASE: if certification_approved = TRUE then earliest_enrollment else NULL

hints: You'll need to combine information from both tables to determine which courses are certified and when their earliest enrollments occurred.

Consider using a LEFT JOIN from courses to a subquery or CTE that computes the minimum enrollment_date per course_id, then use a CASE expression to decide whether to show the date or NULL based on certification status.

The solution structure is: SELECT c.course_id, c.course_name, c.certification_approved, CASE WHEN c.certification_approved THEN e.min_date ELSE NULL END FROM courses c LEFT JOIN (SELECT course_id, MIN(enrollment_date) ... GROUP BY course_id) e ON c.course_id = e.course_id ORDER BY c.course_id.
problem.answer_key: WITH earliest_enrollments AS (SELECT course_id, MIN(enrollment_date) AS min_enrollment_date FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id) SELECT c.course_id, c.course_name, c.certification_approved, CASE WHEN c.certification_approved THEN e.min_enrollment_date ELSE NULL END AS earliest_enrollment FROM courses c LEFT JOIN earliest_enrollments e ON c.course_id = e.course_id ORDER BY c.course_id;

_meta.scenario: an online course platform tracking course completion and certification

user_solution:
/*
Certification-Gated Earliest Enrollment Date Lookup
Prompt
- Find MIN(earliest_enrollment) WHERE certification_approved = TRUE ELSE NULL

OUTPUT
course_id, 
course_name, 
certification_approved, 
earliest_enrollment.

ORDER BY course_id;


Schema
Table: courses
course_id	            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
course_name	            VARCHAR(100)
certification_approved	BOOLEAN

Table: enrollments
enrollment_id	        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
course_id	            INTEGER
student_id	            INTEGER
enrollment_date	        DATE
*/

SELECT
    c.course_id, 
    c.course_name, 
    c.certification_approved, 
    CASE WHEN c.certification_approved = true THEN MIN(e.enrollment_date) ELSE NULL END AS earliest_enrollment
FROM courses AS c
LEFT JOIN enrollments AS e
    USING(course_id)
GROUP BY c.course_id, c.course_name
ORDER BY c.course_id;
